relevance_note: A cohort CNV study of 191 suspected IEI patients that describes one TNFAIP3 carrier with individual-level features: "A monoallelic loss of TNFAIP3 was caused by a heterozygous 59.9 kb deletion in patient-191".
method_note: Hand-built rows assembled by a short Python script; every value read from the paper. Table 1 and Tab.S1/Tab.S2 are present only as captions or images (no cell text), so patient-191's sex, age, onset and other Table-1/Tab.S2 details could not be read and are not reported. Only patient-191 is in scope; the other 190 cohort members (other genes or no CNV) get no rows. The variant is a CNV with no HGVS, transcript or coordinates printed; variant_original_string is the shortest contiguous description ('heterozygous 59.9 kb deletion'). Pathogenicity and variant type come from the Discussion sentence naming patient-191's deletion ('this CNV'). Parental testing: the Limitations paragraph says only in general that 'analysis of the parents would have been helpful to evaluate if aberrations occurred de novo or were inherited'; not specific to patient-191, so inheritance and parental_testing_statement are not reported. The paper never gives patient-191 a disease name (no 'HA20' label; HA20 is mentioned only in general, refs [26-28]), so disease_label_as_stated is not reported; the cohort as a whole had 'a suspected IEI'. is_proband left null (cohort member, not called proband). Checklist 'skin lesions' marked observed from rosacea (a skin finding; not one of the listed examples), 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' observed from lymphadenopathy; chronic sinusitis was not taken as 'recurrent infections'. cites_prior_report is true for patient-005 (ICOS, out of scope), ref [23]. No contradictions found. No stacked cells.
